survivors.q: RB Leipzig reached the Champions League semi-final in 2020. Who knocked them out?
survivors.hint: PSG won the one-off Lisbon semi-final 3-0; Bayern beat Lyon in the other half of the draw and went on to win the trophy.

survivors.q: Timo Werner joined RB Leipzig in 2016, in time for their first Bundesliga season. Which club did he sign from?
survivors.hint: Werner came from boyhood club VfB Stuttgart, who had just been relegated, and promptly scored 21 Bundesliga goals in his first season at Leipzig.

survivors.q: Who was RB Leipzig's head coach when they finished second in their debut Bundesliga season in 2016-17?
survivors.hint: The Austrian arrived in 2016 having just kept newly promoted Ingolstadt in the Bundesliga, and immediately steered Leipzig into the Champions League.

survivors.q: In their first ever DFB-Pokal tie, in 2011, fourth-tier RB Leipzig knocked out a Bundesliga club 3-2. Which one?
survivors.hint: Daniel Frahn scored a first-half hat-trick as Leipzig beat Wolfsburg in front of 31,212 at the Red Bull Arena — the young club's first genuine headline.

survivors.q: When RB Leipzig began playing in 2009, which tier of German football were they in?
survivors.hint: They started in the fifth-tier NOFV-Oberliga Süd and won it at the first attempt, the first of four promotions in seven years.

survivors.q: RB Leipzig were created in 2009 when Red Bull bought the playing rights of which existing club?
survivors.hint: Red Bull paid a reported 350,000 euros for the licence of SSV Markranstädt, a small side from a town just west of Leipzig, and built a new club around it.

survivors.q: Julian Nagelsmann arrived at RB Leipzig in 2019 from which club?
survivors.hint: Nagelsmann made his name at Hoffenheim, where he took charge as a rookie in 2016 and reached the Champions League, before the Leipzig move was agreed a year in advance.

survivors.q: Which player was in RB Leipzig's squad in the third tier in 2013 and was still at the club for their run to the Champions League semi-final in 2020?
survivors.hint: Poulsen joined from Lyngby in 2013 when Leipzig were a 3. Liga side and rose with them all the way; Forsberg, Gulácsi and Orban all arrived in 2015, by which time the club were in the 2. Bundesliga.

survivors.q: Who was RB Leipzig's head coach when they won promotion to the Bundesliga in 2016?
survivors.hint: Rangnick, the club's sporting director and architect, stepped into the dugout himself for the 2015-16 promotion season and then handed the team to Hasenhüttl for the Bundesliga.

survivors.q: Which Germany international played for RB Leipzig in the third and second tiers before Bayern Munich signed him in 2015?
survivors.hint: Kimmich spent two seasons at Leipzig from 2013, and Bayern agreed to buy him in January 2015 — before Leipzig had ever played a Bundesliga game.

survivors.q: Who scored RB Leipzig's winning goal in their 2-1 Champions League quarter-final victory over Atlético Madrid in Lisbon in 2020?
survivors.hint: The American midfielder's deflected strike late on sent Leipzig into a European semi-final for the first time, after João Félix had equalised from the penalty spot.

survivors.q: Who managed RB Leipzig from 2012 until early 2015, winning promotion out of the Regionalliga and then out of the 3. Liga?
survivors.hint: Zorniger's high-pressing side went up in 2013 and again in 2014; he left in early 2015 and was appointed VfB Stuttgart's head coach that summer.

survivors.q: RB Leipzig's full name is RasenBallsport Leipzig rather than Red Bull Leipzig. Why?
o: Another German club already held the rights to the name 'Red Bull Leipzig'
German football's rules did not allow a company name in a club's name
Red Bull wanted the club to look independent so it could receive public money
The city of Leipzig controls what any club using its stadium may call itself
survivors.hint: The invented word 'RasenBallsport' (roughly 'lawn ball sports') exists purely so the initials could stay 'RB' — the club had to engineer a workaround for a restriction on what an official club name is permitted to contain.

survivors.q: RB Leipzig lifted their first major trophy in 2022. Which competition was it?
survivors.hint: The 2022 DFB-Pokal was the club's first silverware of any real weight, and they retained it the following season.

survivors.q: RB Leipzig sold Dominik Szoboszlai in 2023 to which club?
survivors.hint: Liverpool triggered the Hungarian's release clause, following the same Salzburg-to-Leipzig-to-Anfield path Naby Keïta had taken years earlier.

survivors.q: Which defender did RB Leipzig sell to Manchester City in 2023 for a fee that made him one of the most expensive defenders in history?
survivors.hint: Gvardiol arrived from Dinamo Zagreb, starred at the 2022 World Cup for Croatia and moved to City the following summer. Konaté went to Liverpool and Upamecano to Bayern.

survivors.q: In which season did RB Leipzig play their first Bundesliga match?
survivors.hint: Promotion from the 2. Bundesliga in May 2016 put them in the top flight for 2016-17, where they finished second at the first attempt.

survivors.q: Who combined the jobs of sporting director and head coach to take RB Leipzig up to the Bundesliga in 2015-16?
survivors.hint: Rangnick had run the sporting side since 2012 and stepped into the dugout himself for the promotion season, then handed the team over and went back upstairs.

survivors.q: Which coach replaced Domenico Tedesco at RB Leipzig in September 2022 and went on to win the 2023 DFB-Pokal?
survivors.hint: Rose, previously in charge at Salzburg, Mönchengladbach and Dortmund, took over after a poor start to the season and beat Eintracht Frankfurt 2-0 in the following June's final in Berlin.

survivors.q: Which Premier League side did RB Leipzig eliminate 4-0 on aggregate in the 2019-20 Champions League round of 16?
survivors.hint: Nagelsmann's side won 1-0 at Spurs through a Timo Werner penalty and then 3-0 in Leipzig, a tie billed as the young coach against José Mourinho.

survivors.q: In what year was RB Leipzig founded?
survivors.hint: The club was formally founded on 19 May 2009, making it one of the youngest sides ever to reach the Bundesliga.

survivors.q: Atalanta play their home matches in which northern Italian city?
survivors.hint: Atalanta are Bergamo's club through and through: the stadium sits in the Borgo Santa Caterina district and the famous academy is at Zingonia, just outside the city.

survivors.q: In which year was Atalanta founded?
survivors.hint: The club was formed on 17 October 1907 by students of Bergamo's Liceo Classico Paolo Sarpi; a 1920 merger with fellow Bergamo side Bergamasca added the 'Bergamasca' to the name that survives today as Atalanta Bergamasca Calcio.
